name: How much extra does fire separation add to an in-law suite project?

mainEntity.name: How much extra does fire separation add to an in-law suite project?
mainEntity.text: How much extra does fire separation add to an in-law suite project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fire separation is one of the hidden cost drivers in many in-law suite projects. Attached conversions and garage-to-suite projects often need upgraded drywall assemblies, protected openings, rated doors, sealed penetrations, and careful detailing around ceilings and shared walls. If the existing structure is not already compliant, the work can add both materials and labor. The exact cost depends on how much of the current structure can stay and how much must be rebuilt. Homeowners should ask for fire separation to be addressed during design, not after construction starts, because retrofitting code items later usually costs more. This is one of the main reasons a low first estimate can become a much higher final number.
acceptedAnswer.description: Fire separation can add significant cost when walls, ceilings, doors, insulation, and penetrations must be upgraded to meet code. The impact is usually greater in garage conversions and attached suites than in detached units. The final cost depends on what already exists and how much has to be rebuilt.
